text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the CP separation RFC — if we split control plane for private/VPC customers, how do we safely propagate per-tenant routes across a shared peering fabric without leaking routes or blowing route table quotas?

kevin: We need per-tenant route isolation + anti-spoofing. My rough idea: tag routes with tenant-id and only program them into transit routers that host that tenant's sessions. Avoid global route injection.

samir: Cert rotation + auth boundary is the kicker. If controlplanes are separate we need a short-lived attestation token for route sync. Otherwise one compromised CP could register routes elsewhere.

rachel: Also think about scale — AWS RT limits and peering count. If we create per-tenant RTs for everything we'll hit soft limits fast.

kevin: Maybe a hybrid: per-tenant route manifests we push to a shared relay cluster that applies filters and only programs summarized prefixes into global RTs. Per-tenant specifics live behind a tenant-relay.

maria: What's the operator model for failures? If relay loses state do tenants get blackholed? Need clear fail-open/close semantics.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: last smoke: relay-v2 passed in staging. Route-filtering feature flag: off.

leo: Route table quota is real — customers >200 tenants will be painful. Consolidation via aggregation + per-tenant NAT might help.

samir: Proposed spike approach:
1) Signed route manifests from CP -> relay
2) Relay validates signature + tenant ACLs
3) Relay programs per-tenant virtual table and exports aggregates to cloud RTs
Example manifest:
```
tenant: t-12345
prefixes:
 - 10.10.0.0/16
 - 10.11.0.0/16
sig: <base64>
```
This keeps raw per-tenant entries off global RTs.

rachel: Can we do a POC with one customer and measure rt entries + failover behavior? I can take infra side.

maria: Yep — let's spin a 2-week spike. Owners: rachel (infra POC), samir (auth), kevin (relay design). I'll capture in the RFC follow-up doc and schedule a sync. :thumbsup:

kevin: will sketch a sequence diagram and post link here later.
